info:
Arabic has a very important construction:

كنتُ أسبح.
I used to swim / I was swimming.

Literally:

كان = was
أسبح = I swim

This is particularly interesting because كان + present-tense verb can cover both:

I used to swim
I was swimming

info: لم + المضارع المجزوم expresses the past negative; the verb is grammatically present-form أبكِ, not a past-form verb.  Negative statements: Arabic is the major outlier in your set. Past negative statements normally use لم + jussive present-form verb, rather than simply negating the past-tense verb: لم أبكِ (“I did not cry”). For “never,” لم ... قط is common: لم أكتب جيدًا قط (“I never wrote well”).
native_answer: I did not cry before
